To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

&dquo;The interpersonal relationships of people are characterized by four invariant dimensions: Cooperation-Harmony vs. Competition-Conflict, Equality vs. Inequality, Personal- Informal vs. Formal-Distant, and Intimate-Affective vs. Neutral

(a) the dimensions of interpersonal relationships identified in the Wish et al. (1973) research are invariant over different methods of stimulus presentation and different subject groups; and (b) these same dimensions can also be used to describe interpersonal situations.
the four interpersonal dimensions are: (1) cooperation-harmony vs. competition-conflict; (2) equality vs. inequality; (3) personal vs. formal; and (4) intimacy vs. formality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of interpersonal relationships in terms of the dimensions of cooperation, equality, intimacy, and social power.
developing a conceptual and empirical framework for studying and predicting the effects of interpersonal communication on attitudes and behaviors.
the development of a theory of interpersonal communication that can account for the complexity and richness of human interaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the interpersonal communication is a very important and necessary part of the social life.

interpersonal communication can be defined as the exchange of information and meaning among people who are in a relationship with each other, in which the relationship is defined in terms of a set of dimensions, and in which the relationship and the communication are influenced by the situational context.
the interpersonal communication is a complex phenomenon, and the study of it is a complex process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the four dimensions of interpersonal communication are: &dquo;cooperative vs. conflictual,&dquo; and &dquo;equal vs. unequal.&dquo; We are currently working on two other dimensions, which are &dquo;personal vs. formal,&dquo; or &dquo;informal vs. formal,” and ”open vs. closed.” We have also found that the four dimensions are invariant over different stimulus sets.
these dimensions are not merely descriptive but also have predictive value.
we have identified a set of dimensions that are invariant across a wide range of situations, and that these dimensions are related to the structure of the communication process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dimensions of interpersonal communication are not only important in themselves but they also interact with one another.
people are not just responding to the words and actions of others, they are responding to the relationship that exists between them and the others in a given interaction.
interpersonal relationships are characterized by the same dimensions regardless of the method used to study them.
